title.narrative: LI-WAY Addis Abeba Livelihoods Improvements for Women and Youth (2017-24)

description.narrative:
The expected outcome for the 8-year programme is to substantially improve livelihoods for at least 257 000 women and youth in Addis Ababa.
To achieve this, the program facilitates improved employability and increased access to wage and self-employment opportunities for youth and women by working closely with relevant market actors. The program envisages changing market systems so that they work better for poor women and youth in Addis Ababa. In practice, this involves changing the behavior of people and organizations (market actors) within those sectors/market systems. This will help to ensure ownership and scaling by the key market players beyond the project period.
Four organizations in a consortium leads these efforts:
Each consortium partner is responsible for the development of a specific sector:
• SNV leads the consortium and responsible for the micro-enterprises sector development with the objective to reduce constraints of starting & growing MSEs for target groups • Mercy Corpse leads labour market sector development and also manages Innovation Fund with the objective to reduce constraints in input supply & labour productivity • TechnoServe is responsible for medium to large manufacturing firms (growth sector) development; with the objective to reduce constraints in input supply & labour productivity • Save the Children International is responsible for skills market development with the objective to improve standards & quality of skills delivery, and aligned curricula to meet the skills demanded by employers
In addition the RADET intervention introduced in 2022 aims to strengthen the digital entrepreneurship ecosystem by addressing systemic constraints of digital enterprises. More specifically it aims on addressing constraints prioritizing access to finance/business development services and enabling environment (enterprise regulations) i

Insatsen ämnar förbättra sysselsättningsmöjligheterna för minst 200 000 kvinnor och ungdomar i Addis Abeba med närförorter. Initiativet bygger på en väl etablerad ansats för reform av marknadssystem till förmån för fattiga och/eller utsatta grupper, Making Markets Work for the Poor (M4P). Insatsen beräknas pågå under fem år, med ett gåvobistånd på 160 millioner SEK, finansierade av Sida. Fyra internationella enskilda organisationer (NGOs) har identifierats utifrån sin motivation och kapacitet att bidra till implementeringen, med sinsemellan komplementära styrkor och erfarenheter; SNV, TechnoServe (TNS), Mercy Corps och Rädda Barnen. De är alla icke vinstdrivande organisationer, lokalt registrerade som NGOs, som inte bedriver någon kommersiell ekonomisk aktivitet. De är etablerade i Etiopien sedan minst tio år (TNS) och upp till 80 år (Rädda Barnen).
SNV har utifrån kapacitet, relevans och tidigare resultat/erfarenhet utvalts av Sida som ledare för de implementerande parterna ("konsortiet") med totalansvar för implementeringen, varmed de beräknas bli den enda organisation som ingår insatsavtal direkt med Sida. De övriga tre organisationer som beräknas ingå i konsortiet förväntas teckna avtal med SNV som reglerar deras bidrag till implementeringen. Deras huvudsaklinga förväntade bidrag under implementeringen presenteras i en lista i programförslaget (sidan 26), med utgångspunkt i sina institutionella komparativa fördelar. Rädda Barnen bedöms vara starka avseende ungdomssysselsättning och yrkesutbildning, Mercy Corps kombinerar resiliens och marknadsuteckling med goda resultat inom innovativa finansieringslösningar och informationssystem. TNS har gedigen erfarenhet av ungdomssysselsättning och teknologitransfereringar, samt länkar mellan målgruppen och privata sektorns aktörer. SNV har god och bred erfarenhet av värdekedjeprojekt på landsbygden, länkar till resiliens, gender mainstreaming, och gedigen erfarenhet av vidareförmedling av medel. De har också längst och djupast relation till lokala myndigheter, ett område där enbart Rädda Barnen kan mäta sig (och då begränsat till ungdomsfrågor framför allt). Inledande behovsanalyser har identifierat sex marknadssystem av särskild relevans för målgruppen i Addis Ababa, där svagheter på olika nivåer bedöms kunna adresseras genom programmet. De marknadssystem som initialt identifierats som vilktigast för målgruppen är de lokala systemen för yrkesutbildning, kapital, service och tillverkningsindusti, informationssystem samt arbetsmarknadens funktionssätt som helhet i Addis Ababa. Emedan allokeringen av resurser mellan olika aktiviteter kommer att definieras på detaljnivå först under inceptionsfasen, så förväntas samtliga prioriterade aktiviteter under den här ansatsen ha ett drag av facilitering; aktiviteter som underlättar och stimulerar innovation, skapande av plattformar för informationsutbyte mellan olika ekonomiska aktörer, höjer kapaciteten hos arbetsgivare och finansiella institutioner att utveckla produkter och hantera risker unika för målgruppen, och förhandla fram bättre regelverk för målgruppen i arbetslivet lokalt. Olika kapacitetshöjande aktiviteter förväntas därmed stå i centrum för medelsutnyttjandet, medan verktyg av typen "challenge funds" föräntas komma till användning för att stimulera innovation.
Under en inledande inceptionsfas på åtta månader kommer således fördjupade behovs- och aktörsanalyser utföras, och prioriteringar för programmet att göras baserat på den efterfrågan, additionalitet och det mervärde som programmet kan erbjuda. Fördjupade analyser av genomgående prioriterade aspekter såsom miljö och konfliktkänslighet kommer också att göras under inceptionsfasen, emedan etableringen av ett projektkontor färdigställs.
Den fullskaliga implementeringen kommer därefter att utformas med utgångspunkt i inceptionsfasens analyser. Även om detaljer om fokus, ansvars- och medelsfördelning kommer att specificeras mer utvecklat under inceptionsfasen, så finns viktiga hörnstenar definierade för den budget och budgetansats som etablerats till stöd för programmets adaptiva styrning. Budgetallokeringen till administrativa kostander och "overheads" ligger till exempel fast definierad från år till år, och uppgår till 20-25 procent av totalbudgeten beroende på om och hur utvärdering och kunskapsinhämtning (M&E) klassificeras som som "administration" eller inte. Under etiopisk lag kan NGOs inte ådraga sig högre administrativa kostander och "overheads" än maximalt 30 procent. Den "innovationsfond" som förväntas kunna stimulera innovationer i samarbete med kommersiella och icke-kommersiella organisationer beräknas till exempel uppgå till nästan en million euro, 10 millioner SEK, där administration och hantering förväntas ingå i de allmänna administrativa kostanderna som budgeterats för programmet och för värdorganisationen för fonden. Särskilda principer och processbeskrivningar för medelsförmedling har upprättats av SNV och sammanfattats i bifogat utkast till insatsavtal. De kommer att utvecklas vidare när inriktningen på programmet och partneruppställningen finjusteras under inceptionsfasen.
Efterhand årliga aktivitetsplaner fastställs och budgeteras enligt den adaptiva styrningsmodellens principer, kommer budgetbehoven att beaktas vid bedömning av utbetalningstakt och -tidpunkt under året.

This contribution aims at improving the livelihoods conditions for at least 200,000 women and youth in the greater Addis Abeba region. The initiative builds on a well-established approach to pro-poor market systems reform (Making Markets Work for the Poor, M4P). The contribution is expected to be implemented over five years, with a 160 million SEK grant from Sida. Four international NGOs have been identified to have capacity and interest in contributing to the implementation, all with different and complementary strengths and experiences. The four institutions, SNV, TechnoServe, Mercy Corps and Save the Children, are engaged through sub-agreements with SNV, who is Sida’s agreement partner and lead implementing agency in the consortium. Throughout an inception phase and an implementation phase, the consortium partners are expected to undertake a range of facilitation activities to stimulate better performance among stakeholders in the market systems in Addis Abeba which are important for poor women and youth. From an initial set of assumptions stemming from primary analysis, the exact paths to reaching the overall objectives will evolve dynamically in an adaptive management process.

LIWAY continues to show impressive results exploring new and innovative approaches to work with privates sector, government and other market actors to improve incomes and create jobs for the target groups. To date, LIWAY has partnered with 172 market actors (65 public and 107 private) to deliver 57 live and completed interventions and has mobilised a total of 344.6 million ETB since the start of the programme. Of this, 50.4 million ETB is from partners in this reporting period.
During the reporting period, LIWAY facilitated employment and income for 92,267 target group members, which is a 79% increase from the programme results achieved up to the end of 2022. To date, the programme has facilitated the creation of increased jobs and incomes for 170,161 target group members, of which 95,138 (56% of the total) are women (young and adult) and 138,243 (81% of the total) are youth (female and male). The overall results are driven most significantly by the MSE system (41%) followed by the skills system (23%).
Integration for greater impact
Efforts are being made by the consortium partners to work across the different systems. One notable example is the partnership between the MSE system and the skills system, which have joined forces with a private company to empower home-based women through targeted skills training and market linkages. This intervention has begun impacting several targets, empowering over 1,500 home-based women and janitors by providing them with job opportunities and increased income.
Collaborative efforts for systemic impact.
The programme's interventions, implemented through all its IPs, have begun to attract the attention of development institutions, as well as national and international private actors working in similar spaces. Recent engagements have focused on the potential adaptation of LIWAY's Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Bazaar for MSEs and Fostering Market-Based Employment Opportunities for refugees, migrants, and internally displaced persons.
GESI Intergration
LIWAY has implemented various strategies to ensure the participation of women and individuals with physical challenges. These strategies include setting targets and incorporating them into contract agreements with IPs. However for greater impact private sector Implementing patners need to see the business case in order to monitor these outcomes.
Advocacy Inititatives: Some examples on advocacy initiatives that address skills mismatch and the inefficiencies in the TVET system include
-Higher Education, Technical and Vocational Training, Research Institution, and Industry Linkage Proclamation, which permits TVET trainers to participate in industry attachment programmes.
-The Training and Education Policy now mandates vocational and pedagogy skills for TVET trainers.
-Drectives addressing TVET internal assessment implementation, occupational competency recognition and certification, vocational guidance and counselling, and cooperative training.
Progress Towards Systemic Change using the Adopt, Adapt, Expand and Replicate Framework (AAER) in the 4 sytems
The four systems all show clear signs of progress contributing towards systemic change.
Adopt : Different actors changing different behaviours which leads to impact with LIWAY support
LABOUR:Rays Microfinance Institution and HudHud PLC implemented item-based digital loans to serve MSEs.
SMES: Totos Kenya (TTK) successfully replicated a childcare model from Kenya to Ethiopia, adding 12 childcare/daycare facilities to enhance quality and business. This initiative is expected to drive positive outcomes by adopting proven models from other contexts. Ashewa embraced the business model for the e-commerce intervention and made the strategic choice to focus on MLEs in addition to its current MSE customer categories.
SKILLS:Aha Psychological Service implemented an intervention to address the issue of employability readiness of targets. Aha supported 12 TVET colleges with vocational and counselling guidance (VGC) services and continued delivering the service at its premises. Aha also offered ToT for 19 officers on the design and delivery of VGC services in their respective colleges, and more than 30 TVET experts were capacitated to support the process and launch the services in targeted colleges.
Adapt: actors continuing and adapting these behaviours without LIWAY support accross the 4 systems
LABOUR: Masero has adapted its recruitment platform with strategic enhancements in candidate screening, recruiter collaboration, and data tracking methods, expanding geographically into Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania. The platform's media recognition and 156% growth in job matching success signify successful adaptation to dynamic market forces.
SME: In 2023, HellooMarket upgraded various components of the existing e-commerce system, such as design, functionality, and content to improve the experience of customers and suppliers and to remain competitive in the market (e.g., make it easier to manage stock, add or remove products, calculate taxes, and process orders). The continuous improvement of the platform and the real-time feedback provided by customers to suppliers have resulted in improved product standardisation and quality. HellooMarket is also working on integrating its system with online payments such as Telebirr and other platforms to facilitate various in-country and international payments.
MLE: The recent results survey of 11 MLEs (Booez Food Complex, Anbessa Shoe SC, Kebron Flour, Alemayehu Nigussie Metal Packaging, Crane PLC, Moplaco Trading PLC, Yahenu PLC, Moyee Coffee, Gast Solar Mechanics, Flexible packaging and Horizon Plantation) that adopted the production management intervention (1st and advanced level kaizen) showed that most MLEs have continued implementing Kaizen (Quality and Productivity ImprovementQPI) practices, and other production management efficiency tools for 71 employees and managers across the MLEs. All 11 MLEs have benefited from the intervention in multiple ways, including through increased productivity, installed capacity utilisation, sales volume, revenue, and profit, as well as notable cost reductions, resulting in the creation of new jobs to support their business expansions.
SKILLS: The workforce development for leather companies in partnership with MIDI has been implemented and sustained by the three companies. The companies owned the training centres and made them part of the institutional annual key priorities, - they budgeted annually and assigned trainers and coordinators exclusively for the centre. Moreover, the companies established and institutionalised strategic plans where they can regularly identify staff skills gaps, plan the agreed and identified training areas, and carry out training and certify the trained staff, which enables them to upgrade their roles and range of responsibility, therefore improving their salaries and benefits.
Expand : more people benefitting from the intervention to a greater extent through expansion and replication
LABOUR: The entry of innovative platforms like Myjobs and SabiJobs transforms the industry, fostering healthy competition and service quality enhancements. Adoption of successful childcare models by industrial parks and the establishment of public childcare centres signal a significant trend, increasing job opportunities and service accessibility.
SMEs: BelCash Technology Solutions has expanded the digital marketing services outside Addis Ababa to the Tigray, Somali, and Sidama regions and with new collaborators to Amhara and Afar. The business model has also been copied by different emulators such as Ashewa, CommercePal, and Shega, among others, who have all begun providing services for target MSEs in addition to medium and large enterprises. As a result, the intervention has impacted around 20,000 enterprises across the board.
MLEs: The production management intervention is gradually expanding. During the reporting period, five additional private consulting service providers entered the market by replicating the business model while the Global Kaizen Institute started work in Ethiopia using four certified private consultants who were trained through the intervention. Furthermore, four non-targeted MLEs (1 outside of Addis Ababa) and one company from the services sector purchased a process and production management consultancy service from the implementing partners, indicating that the market is expanding its services reach.
Response: Other market actors changing their behaviours in response to the market changes
LABOUR: Government's Digital Overseas Employment Initiative: Government's collaboration with key market players, including job matching services and private employment agencies, coupled with TVET college partnerships for soft-skills training, demonstrates a robust response. MoUs with destination market country embassies and One Stop Service centers highlight a strong commitment to facilitate overseas employment.
SMES: LIWAY has influenced changes in policies based on evidence generated from different interventions. For example, the e-commerce proclamation (2020) is responding to a wide range of constraints of e-commerce operation. BelCash played a crucial role in developing the e-commerce proclamation by being part of the drafting committee as a pioneer in e-commerce platform development. The proclamation brought significant changes to the e-commerce landscape. According to Ethiopian law, the next step is to issue the regulation. To that end, the Ministry of Innovation and Technology (MINT) has drafted the e-regulation and submitted it to the Council of Ministers for approval. BelCash continues to influence policy, such as for enactment of Ethiopian Revenues and Customs Authority (ERCA) invoice on delivery policy that is relevant for rules on e-commerce compliance.
MLEs: The market has already responded to the waste recycling business model in 2022. Additional signs from non-competing market players further solidify the stage of the market. The sector has attracted the attention of many non-competing market players supporting the core market actors. For example, logistics providers (transport service providers) are amongst the supporting functions that have increasingly entered the market, providing a critical service to the core waste recycling businesses. The sector has also caught the eye of other development agencies, local and international, who are working to improve the waste recycling ecosystem, including GIZ, ILO, First Consult and PETCO. In response to the markets need for waste collection guidelines, AACMA implemented a procedure that encourages the sustainable collection and segregation of wastepaper by home-to-home collectors and prohibits the disposal of wastepaper in landfills.
SKILLS: Work ethics training has been integrated in the TVET curriculum and is being delivered to trainees. Integration of soft skills training in the TVET technical curriculum was indicated in the upcoming TVET policy. Further, The Federal TVET Institute endorsed a course of soft skills training for TVET trainers and started delivering the training to TVET trainers, who are cascading it to TVET trainees.
The program is highly likely to improve incomes through enhanced wage and self-employment opportunities for the targeted 257,000 people, primarily youth and women, as evidenced by the exponential trajectory of the achieved results. The program continues through 2024.
